To solve the inequality 

$$
-{x}^{2}+9x-18\ge 0,
$$

we need to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola 

$$
y=-{x}^{2}+9x-18
$$

lies *above* the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

First, let's find the roots of the parabola:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+9x-18 & =0 \\ -({x}^{2}-9x+18) & =0 \\ -(x-3)(x-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the roots are $x=3$ and $x=6,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/d4c28d26425c3c5bfc95dece73c8d8cb74f395f2de04a2c2ee1b1fd69f8433ed.png)

The values marked in blue show all $x$-values where the parabola lies *above* the axis or touches the $x$-axis. 

So, the solution to the inequality is $3\le x\le 6.$
